answer:
The feature is **iterative index scans**, available starting with pgvector 0.8.0. "Starting with 0.8.0, you can enable iterative index scans, which will automatically scan more of the index until enough results are found (or it reaches `hnsw.max_scan_tuples` or `ivfflat.max_probes`)." [pgvector/README.md]

Your symptom happens because "queries with filtering can return less results since filtering is applied *after* the index is scanned." [pgvector/README.md]

To enable it for HNSW, set the scan mode in your session. Strict ordering returns results in exact distance order: "SET hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order;" [pgvector/README.md]

Relaxed ordering allows slightly out-of-order results in exchange for better recall: "SET hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order;" The README also shows "SET ivfflat.iterative_scan = relaxed_order;" for IVFFlat indexes. [pgvector/README.md]

The README doesn't say how the scan limits interact with your specific LIMIT, so I can't confirm more detail than this.
